commits.message:
fix(text): review — tab size is checked, Constrain/Align measure as Rich does, whitespace keeps its width (rich-text-z3ln)

expandTabs refuses a tabSize that is not a positive integer (it silently
dropped spans at 0) and measures a piece only when a tab follows it.
Constrain measures its content at the constrained width; Align returns the
content's measurement unchanged. Whitespace-only text takes its width as
its minimum, as in Rich.

fix(text): measurement agrees with what is drawn (rich-text-z3ln)

- RichText.measure takes its minimum from wrap's `widestWord`, the same word
  `divideLine` never breaks, so a line's indent counts. Deliberate divergence
  from Rich, whose measure drops the indent its wrapper keeps.
- One `expandTabs` in cells.ts, called by RichText and Syntax: a tab reaches the
  next tab stop (Rich's `Text.expand_tabs`). It also maps offsets, so a span
  after a tab now styles the characters it named instead of landing short.
- No site outside `Measurement.get` decides the fallback for a renderable that
  cannot measure itself. Viewport and Constrain floored that minimum at 1;
  it is now Rich's 0.

fix(traceback)!: render any caught value and every V8 frame shape (rich-traceback-9vcb) (#293)

* fix(traceback): render any caught value and every V8 frame shape (rich-traceback-9vcb)

Traceback takes unknown and reads a caught value by shape in browser-safe
code (string name + message is an error; anything else is NonError,
formatted by Pretty), replacing installTraceback's node:util toError.

Frames: the stack's own header is stripped before frames are read, so a
message line is never a frame; frames with no line (Promise.all index,
<anonymous>, native) keep their location; eval frames show the eval
site's file; SpiderMonkey/JSC stacks are read; an unreadable line shows
verbatim. The data bounds print uses move to pretty.ts as
UNSEEN_DATA_BOUNDS so Traceback shares them.

* fix(traceback): survive throwing reads, keep an error's name, read node's coded header (rich-traceback-9vcb)

High-review fixes: a value whose name/message/stack read throws is reported
under NonError where Pretty marks the throw, instead of throwing out of the
crash handler; a non-string message is formatted by Pretty under the error's
own name; node's `Name [ERR_X]: message` header comes off whole; a stale
header with no V8 frame shows no frame; a NonError value is laid out in the
width left after its name.

* fix(traceback): a stale header is read by its shape, not the error's current name (rich-traceback-9vcb)
